# 0.1 C++ for CP: I/O, types, overflow, compiling, online judges

Phase 0 (Foundations), target rating 800–1000. Bank status: not started.

## Patterns

### Large input and output (`fast-io`)

Read or print up to about 10^6 numbers, where the speed of the stream calls decides whether the program finishes in time.

**Works because:** The input or output volume is large enough that unsynchronised C++ streams (or many separate flushes) become the bottleneck, while the algorithm itself is linear.

### 64-bit arithmetic (`overflow-64bit`)

Sums or products exceed 2^31 − 1, so 32-bit int silently overflows; the fix is long long in the right places.

**Works because:** The largest intermediate value is above about 2.1·10^9 but below about 9.2·10^18, so long long holds it exactly.

### Many test cases (`multi-test`)

One input file holds many test cases; all state must be reset per test and the work per test must be proportional to that test's size.

**Works because:** The statement bounds the sum of n over all tests, so O(n) work per test is O(total n) overall, but clearing a fixed-size global array per test is not.

### Exact integer formulas (`integer-rounding`)

Ceilings, floors, and divisions done with integer formulas such as (a + b − 1) / b instead of floating point.

**Works because:** All quantities are integers, so an exact integer formula exists and avoids floating-point rounding errors on large values.
